info.title: MailCheckr API
info.description: Explainable email verification with conservative results (PRD §8). Quick mode checks syntax, domain/DNS/MX routing and local risk datasets and never claims a mailbox was tested. Deep SMTP mode is RELEASE-GATED and currently BLOCKED — outbound TCP/25 is unapproved/untested from the production worker environment (Phase 0 gate), so mode="deep" returns Quick evidence capped at `likely_valid` with reason `smtp_port_unavailable`, never `valid`, and no SMTP traffic is sent. This service never sends email and never issues the SMTP DATA command. `unknown` results and duplicate rows are never charged. This document is served live by the API at GET /v1/openapi.json and kept in the repo at docs/openapi.json; a route-coverage test (apps/api/test/openapi.test.ts) fails if any controller route is missing from it.

get.description: Process liveness only (operational endpoint, outside the versioned product contract). Does not claim database/queue health it has not checked.

Returns the machine-readable OpenAPI 3.1 specification (docs/openapi.json in the repository) describing every route this API exposes. Public so integrators and tooling can fetch it without credentials.

post.description: Creates a user and their single workspace, grants the provisional free credits via a ledger `grant` entry, and returns a session JWT. Passwords are stored only as bcrypt hashes; passwords must be at least 10 characters.
Verifies credentials against the stored password hash. Unknown user and wrong password return the same INVALID_CREDENTIALS error (no account enumeration).
Records the logout in the audit log. Sessions are stateless JWTs, so clients must also discard the token; server-side revocation is a documented production hardening step.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing/invalid JWT or API key.

get.description: Requires a user-session JWT (an API key has no user identity and is rejected).

401.description: Unauthorized — missing/invalid JWT or API key.

post.description: Always returns ok:true, whether or not the email belongs to an account (no enumeration). The reset token is stored only as a SHA-256 hash and expires after 1 hour. Delivery requires a transactional mail provider: MailCheckr never sends email itself, so in non-production the token is additionally returned as `devResetToken` for local testing; in production a provider integration must deliver it.
Consumes a single-use reset token and sets a new password (minimum 10 characters). Invalid/expired/used tokens return RESET_TOKEN_INVALID.

Quick mode (default): syntax/normalisation + domain/DNS/MX + local risk datasets. It never claims the individual mailbox was checked — a passing address is `likely_valid` with reason `smtp_not_attempted_quick_mode`. Deep mode (mode="deep") is RELEASE-GATED and currently BLOCKED: outbound TCP/25 has not been tested/approved from any production worker (PRD Phase 0 / §6), so SMTP_DEEP_ENABLED and SMTP_EGRESS_APPROVED are both false. While the gate is off, a deep request is NOT simulated and never returns `valid`: it returns the Quick (syntax/DNS/risk) classification capped at `likely_valid` with reason code `smtp_port_unavailable`. No SMTP DATA command is ever issued by this service, in any mode. Charging (PRD §9): one credit for a billable terminal result; `unknown` results are NOT charged; a repeated `idempotency_key` returns the original record without re-executing or re-charging. Rate-limited per tenant.

post.summary: Create and process a batch of email addresses
post.description: JSON batch (cap: 1,000 emails per request). Rows are deduplicated on the normalised address: duplicates point at the canonical row and are NOT charged; `unknown` outcomes are NOT charged. In the API-only runtime the batch is processed synchronously before responding; in the full deployment the identical processing runs in the BullMQ worker (apps/worker) and the batch is polled via GET /v1/batches/{id}. Batch creation is rate-limited per workspace (default 5/hour). Deep mode (mode="deep") is RELEASE-GATED and currently BLOCKED: outbound TCP/25 has not been tested/approved from any production worker (PRD Phase 0 / §6), so SMTP_DEEP_ENABLED and SMTP_EGRESS_APPROVED are both false. While the gate is off, a deep request is NOT simulated and never returns `valid`: it returns the Quick (syntax/DNS/risk) classification capped at `likely_valid` with reason code `smtp_port_unavailable`. No SMTP DATA command is ever issued by this service, in any mode.

delete.description: Requires a user-session JWT — an API key is refused with 403, and only the workspace owner may delete. API callers may send {"confirmation":"DELETE"} (validated when present); the dashboard gates client-side by typing DELETE and sends no body. This is a verified purge, not a deferred request: batches, verification records, batch rows and API keys are deleted, credit-ledger entries and amounts are retained with links severed, an audit event is written, and the workspace and user are deleted.

403.description: API-key callers and non-owners are refused.

bearerJwt.description: Dashboard session JWT from POST /v1/auth/register or /v1/auth/login.

bearerApiKey.description: Programmatic API key: Authorization: Bearer mc_live_<secret>. Shown once at creation, stored only as a keyed hash, revocable, scoped. Never put API keys in query strings (PRD §8.1).

VerificationStatus.description: Canonical mailbox status (PRD §4.2). `valid` means only that the target MX accepted the recipient at the SMTP RCPT stage with a conclusive non-catch-all result; it is never reachable while Deep SMTP is gated off. `duplicate` is deliberately absent: it is a row-level disposition, not a mailbox status.

ReasonCode.description: Stable machine-readable reason code (PRD §4.3 plus catch_all_unchecked from §4.6). Every result carries at least one.

Confidence.description: Qualitative evidence-strength label only (PRD §4.4) — NOT a statistical probability, and there is deliberately no numeric score anywhere in this API.

VerificationMode.description: quick = syntax + DNS/MX + local risk datasets (mailbox not tested). deep = SMTP RCPT-stage probe, release-gated and currently BLOCKED (see the mode=deep notes on the verification operations).

Checks.description: Per-check outcomes actually observed. smtp_mailbox is `not_checked` in Quick mode and while the Deep gate is off.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code, e.g. VALIDATION_ERROR, UNAUTHORIZED, NOT_FOUND, INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS, RATE_LIMITED.

ErrorEnvelope.description: The single error shape for every endpoint (PRD §8.6). Raw SMTP transcripts and stack traces are never returned.

devResetToken.description: Non-production only: the plaintext reset token, returned so the flow is testable locally. Never present in production responses.

mode.description: Defaults to quick. deep is release-gated/BLOCKED: while the gate is off the result is capped at likely_valid with reason smtp_port_unavailable and is never `valid`.

idempotency_key.description: Client-generated unique key; retries return the original result without re-charging.

explanation.description: Human-readable explanation of exactly what was and was not checked.

VerificationResult.description: A single verification result (PRD §4.3/§8.2): status, evidence strength, checks performed, reason codes and an honest explanation. DNS evidence and SMTP evidence are distinguishable via `checks` and `reason_codes`; there is no numeric score.

webhook_url.description: Accepted for forward compatibility; webhooks are P1 and the field is inert in the MVP (never silently treated as live).

status.description: Mailbox status, or `duplicate` for a row-level duplicate (result fields then mirror the canonical row; never charged).

secret.description: The full mc_live_… secret. Returned exactly once, at creation; it is stored only as a keyed hash and cannot be recovered.

quantity.description: Signed quantity per the ledger convention (charges are negative).
